text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Japan crushes India and Australia humiliated by Portugal in vote at United Nations for seats on UN Security Council.
- Nixon Center for Peace and Freedom, non-profit public policy institution, names Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew for its "Architect of the New Century" award this year.
- Stockbroker Rashid Hussain Bhd in talks to acquire Malayan banking Bhd subsidiary Kwong Yik Bank.
- Singapore Telecom may get higher weighting in Morgan Stanley Capital International's Singapore Index after government's recent sale of second tranche of shares.
- Five recently listed companies dominate actives list on stock exchange.
- Manufacturing, wholesale and distribution group Ossia International Pte Ltd gets stock exchange approval for initial public offer.
- Surprise earlier 'ready' trading in Labroy's shares will begin today, while for Delifrance 'ready' trading starts on Friday.
- Beijing orders Guangdong province to act on 31 failed projects involving Hongkong $16 billion.
- Economists bring down forecasts of Singapore economic growth to 3 percent for third quarter and 6.5 percent for full year.
- Defence questions Rajabali Jumabhoy, patriarch of Scotts Holdings group, on share transfer.
- Hongkong-listed property developer Guangzhou Investment hails land price cuts as 'positive' to future performance.
